heading: Networks often learn real patterns before memorizing noisy labels
definition: networks fit the patterns shared by real data before memorizing noisy or random labels, so real and random labels are learned differently over training (Arpit et al. 2017).
summary: Several independent groups reproduce earlier learning of clean labels followed by later noise memorization under random label corruption. This ordering can fail with structured or adversarial noise, very high corruption, and some synthetic tasks.

suggested_status.by_scale: Toy: R2 with restricted counterexamples (noisy-XOR ReLU theory and ReLU modular addition challenge the order); <1B: R2 except at very high noise, where pretrained wav2vec2.0 large (317.38M per 10.18653/2026.findings-emnlp.1693#R23) at 5% training scale and 90% replacement challenges it; 1–10B: R0 for the corrected 8B LoRA setting; 10–100B: ?; >100B: ?. The 1–10B assessment follows corrected pack evidence absent from the automated size buckets. The scope-limiting pair, asymmetric, feature-dependent, BadLabel and very-high-noise MNIST results have no stated parameter counts and are not placed on the scale.
suggested_status.reason: R2 applies to conditional earlier clean-label fitting followed by later noisy-label fitting. Reviewed, controlled results report this ordering for ResNet-34/CIFAR-10 with 40% corruption (arXiv:2002.10319#R6) and VGG-16/CIFAR-100 with 50% permutation (arXiv:2105.14602#R3, arXiv:2105.14602#R4). MNIST MLP trajectories provide explicitly sized small-model evidence (arXiv:2611.04199#R7, arXiv:2611.04199#R8). Corrected LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct single-LoRA rows provide qualitative evidence on Trec with 20% asymmetric noise (arXiv:2510.10208#R1, arXiv:2510.10208#R2). Scope after the checks: R2 is not established for the following conditions, where at least one study reports overlapping, simultaneous or reversed clean/noisy learning. (1) Pair noise: with 30% pair flips the digits MLP has memorized 47.1 ± 11.9% of corrupted labels when 95% of clean examples are fitted (10.55529/jaimlnn.62.84.97#R32, 10.55529/jaimlnn.62.84.97#R33; limits_scope); Prestopping qualifies the separation under pair noise in text only (arXiv:1911.08059; limits_scope). (2) Asymmetric noise: AutoTSP reports substantial noisy learning from the initial stages for ResNet110 on CIFAR-100 with 40% asymmetric noise (arXiv:2012.13435, Section V-A/Figure 6, rowless; limits_scope). (3) Feature-dependent noise: ResNet32 with Pseudo noise (CIFAR-10 at 0.2, CIFAR-100 at 0.5) fits clean and noisy examples from the beginning (arXiv:2105.10796#R10, arXiv:2105.10796#R12; challenges after the checks). (4) Adversarial BadLabel: on CIFAR-10 with 40% BadLabel, noisy labels have lower losses than clean labels at epoch 5 (arXiv:2305.18377#R1; challenges), and the rowless DivideMix epoch-10 comparison (Section 3.5/Figure 1(d)) reports nearly indistinguishable losses, interpreted as failure of early learning (challenges after the checks). (5) Very high noise: MNIST learning is dominated by mislabeled data especially above ρ=0.85 (arXiv:2101.06509, Section 4, rowless; limits_scope); pretrained wav2vec2.0 large at 5% training scale and 90% replacement reaches 29.8% peak test accuracy while exception memorization approaches 100% (10.18653/2026.findings-emnlp.1693#R23; challenges after the checks). (6) Synthetic theory settings: the noisy-XOR two-layer ReLU network fits clean and flipped training labels at the first step, before generalizable features emerge (arXiv:2310.02541#R1, arXiv:2310.02541#R2; challenges), and a smaller-step-size XOR experiment shows the same overfitting-then-generalization order (arXiv:2310.02541#R4; challenges); ReLU modular addition with 30% label noise reaches high clean and noisy training accuracy before decay and grokking (arXiv:2610.11833, Appendix D.3/Figure 15, rowless; challenges). The level is unchanged because none of these is a failed replication under matched conventional-noise conditions. Where the same studies use symmetric or randomized noise, they report the clean-first order (arXiv:2105.10796#R9, arXiv:2105.10796#R11 with Randomized noise; 10.55529/jaimlnn.62.84.97#R29, 10.55529/jaimlnn.62.84.97#R30 with 40% symmetric noise; the rowless symmetric-noise DivideMix comparison of arXiv:2305.18377). The two very-high-noise results do use random noise, but at rates above those at which the same studies report the clean-first order (10.18653/2026.findings-emnlp.1693#R21, 10.18653/2026.findings-emnlp.1693#R22 at the same 5% training scale with 10% and 70% replacement; arXiv:2101.06509#R1, arXiv:2101.06509#R3 including 50% noise). The XOR and modular-addition results use synthetic data and training setups unlike the conventional-noise experiments. Supportive results also exist under some out-of-scope conditions (arXiv:1911.08059#R1 with 40% pair noise; arXiv:2510.10208#R1, arXiv:2510.10208#R2 with 20% asymmetric noise; the rowless instance-dependent DivideMix comparison of arXiv:2305.18377), so the evidence there is mixed. arXiv:2105.10796, 10.18653/2026.findings-emnlp.1693 and arXiv:2305.18377 share no authors with an original. Counts were built before the checks and include none of their reclassifications: versions.V6.verdicts.supports.studies=141, versions.V6.studies_with_limits_scope=28, versions.V6.studies_with_challenges=3, and versions.V6.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original=4. The packs give V6 challenges verdicts to arXiv:2305.18377, arXiv:2310.02541 and arXiv:2610.11833; the checks reclassified the limits_scope verdicts of arXiv:2105.10796 (Pseudo noise), 10.18653/2026.findings-emnlp.1693 (90% replacement) and arXiv:2305.18377 (DivideMix/BadLabel epoch 10) as challenges, so neither the challenges count nor the limits_scope count is a corrected total. These counts describe the evidence pool, rather than establishing universal validity or independence for every study.
suggested_status.open_questions: A failed replication under matched conventional-noise conditions, or evidence that the reported ordering is a measurement artifact, would support C. Independent replication of the corrected 8B setting would strengthen its scale-specific level. Direct trajectories at 10–100B and >100B would address missing scale coverage. Causal isolation of shared-pattern acquisition remains needed to establish that part of the wording. Further tests under pair, asymmetric and feature-dependent noise, adversarial BadLabel and very high noise would show whether these scope limits hold across groups and models, and so whether the statement needs a narrower wording or separate versions.

source.title: A Closer Look at Memorization in Deep Networks
source.authors: Devansh Arpit; Stanislaw Jastrzebski; Nicolas Ballas; D. Krueger; Emmanuel Bengio; Maxinder S. Kanwal; Tegan Maharaj; Asja Fischer; Aaron C. Courville; Yoshua Bengio; Simon Lacoste-Julien

original_result.setup: Arpit et al. trained CNNs on CIFAR-10 and MLPs on MNIST with 20% to 80% random label replacement.
original_result.result: Both experiments reported training and validation accuracy curves. The results are graphical, without numerical estimates of the separation between clean-label learning and noise memorization.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

wording_issues.phrase: before memorizing noisy or random labels
wording_issues.issue: “Before” can imply nonoverlapping learning phases. The MNIST MLP learns real and random-label examples concurrently despite fitting real examples earlier. ResNet-9 has overlapping stable-learning times, especially with Adam. ResNet32 with feature-dependent Pseudo noise on CIFAR-10 at corruption fraction 0.2 and CIFAR-100 at 0.5 substantially fits both clean and noisy examples from the beginning: the claimed clean-first, noise-later sequence is absent in these conditions. The digits MLP also shows overlapping clean fitting and pair-flip memorization.

wording_issues.phrase: networks fit the patterns shared by real data before memorizing noisy or random labels
wording_issues.issue: The order reverses or is absent in restricted settings. On CIFAR-10 with 40% BadLabel corruption, lower noisy-label losses at epoch 5 are explicitly interpreted as noisy labels being fitted first; nearly indistinguishable DivideMix losses at epoch 10 are also presented as failure of early learning. The XOR ReLU analysis fits all supplied training labels before generalizable features emerge. The modular-addition ReLU setting with 30% label noise, λ=0.001 and γ=0.1 reports memorization before later grokking. Its separate GELU row shows faster initial noisy-example loss decrease, which cannot determine shared-pattern-before-noise ordering.

The unqualified subject includes regimes without a separate late noisy-classification phase. The smoothed-leaky-ReLU guarantee classifies every clean and corrupted training point correctly after the first gradient step. Class-imbalanced CIFAR-10 can favor an observed class rather than clean labels. Selected Late Stopping examples learn their wrong labels earlier than their corrected alternatives. In wav2vec2.0 large tone classification at 5% training scale and 90% label replacement, corrupted labels are fitted directly without a reliable preceding abstraction phase; this challenges the predicted ordering in that condition.

ResNet-34 and PreAct ResNet-18 clean/noisy accuracy or loss trajectories establish differential fitting without directly identifying shared patterns. Circuit-fault sensitivity is another indirect measurement. DenseNet feature visualizations supply qualitative representation evidence but do not isolate its causal role.

Later memorization is conditional on training procedure, dataset and observation window. CAR reportedly prevents false-label memorization; DAL keeps wrong-label accuracy low; RLL maintains preference for original labels throughout training; the ImageNet-PI cross-entropy baseline ignores wrong labels within its observed budget.

The included noise types are not interchangeable. MNIST regression with structured additive noise depends on noise frequency: Figures 4a–b vary amplitude β at fixed k=0.1 and k=1, respectively; separate frequency sweeps fix β=0.5 or β=1. Gaussian continuous targets differ from random classification labels. ResNet32 with feature-dependent Pseudo noise on CIFAR-10 at corruption fraction 0.2 and CIFAR-100 at 0.5 fits clean and noisy examples substantially from the beginning, challenging the claimed sequence. DeepLab-v1/PASCAL VOC foreground categories are plotted separately; noisy-label agreement alone cannot establish ordering. Early ground-truth recovery followed by decline is reported for most foreground categories, with different timing. Highly structured repeated segmentation errors may prevent early recovery, according to a tentative text-based qualification.

wording_issues.phrase: real and random labels are learned differently over training
wording_issues.issue: Separate real-label and random-label experiments support a dynamics distinction in st-VGG and ResNet-18. Those comparisons do not establish within-mixture ordering. Conversely, the ResNet-34 and two-layer CNN mixed-corruption results do not themselves establish a matched comparison of wholly clean and wholly random-label training runs.

Held-out deterioration and fixed-checkpoint prediction differences do not directly establish individual noisy-label memorization over time. Skin-lesion and RaFD evidence relies on held-out performance; the CIFAR-10 probe establishes differential fitting at one checkpoint; ER segmentation test-Dice collapse supplies an indirect temporal indicator.

wording_issues.phrase: fit the patterns shared by real data before memorizing
wording_issues.issue: Some supportive measurements establish only part of the sequence. WideResNet early accuracy and early-stopped ResNet-20 loss distributions do not independently demonstrate later noise memorization. Mixed retinal noise establishes early correct-pattern learning without later low-quality-label fitting. Infant-pose loss separation establishes different dynamics without the complete sequence.

method_sensitivity.factor: Noise mechanism and dependence on inputs
method_sensitivity.what: BadLabel on CIFAR-10 at 40% corruption produces lower noisy-example losses at epoch 5, interpreted by the authors as noisy labels fitted first. Its rowless DivideMix comparison at epoch 10 reports nearly indistinguishable losses and failure of early learning under BadLabel; the conventional-noise comparison is also rowless. ResNet32 fits clean and noisy examples substantially from the beginning under feature-dependent Pseudo noise at corruption fractions 0.2 on CIFAR-10 and 0.5 on CIFAR-100, challenging V6; matched Randomized noise delays noisy learning. The digits MLP shows separated phases with 40% symmetric noise and overlapping phases with 30% pair flips, changing noise rate as well as structure. Source-generated adaptation noise begins being memorized within one epoch, versus several epochs for replacements restricted to initially mislabeled samples.

CAR with target correction reportedly prevents later false-label memorization in modified ResNet34/CIFAR-10 with 40% symmetric noise; continued clean-label learning alone does not establish V6. On CIFAR-100 with 40% instance-dependent noise, CE ResNet18 eventually reaches 100% wrong-label accuracy, GCE rises late, and DAL keeps wrong-label accuracy low. GCE's stated comparison with MAE is internally inconsistent; no repaired comparison with CE is asserted. Inception-Lite/CIFAR-10 with CCE learns original labels preferentially early, then fits altered labels; the MSE comparison belongs to ResNet-18/MNIST. RLL maintains higher original-label than noisy-label accuracy throughout training. On tested CIFAR-10 and MNIST symmetric-flipping settings, standard training learns incorrect labels rapidly after epoch 60 and closes the gap by epoch 100; adversarial training learns them more slowly and retains a gap at epoch 100, supporting V6's differentiated learning order.

method_sensitivity.factor: Learning rate, schedule and observation duration
method_sensitivity.what: Cosine annealing slows false-label memorization relative to MultiStep for cross-entropy ResNet34/CIFAR-10 at 40% symmetric noise. Clean and noisy trajectories jointly support V6 under each schedule; clean-label accuracy alone does not establish ordering. Residual-network CIFAR-100/ImageNet experiments separate clean/noisy losses at large learning rates; the authors report mislabeled-example fitting after further learning-rate reduction. A rowless CIFAR-100 ResNet-18 comparison reports high noisy loss at constant learning rate 0.1 versus faster noise fitting at 0.001. In abstaining VGG-16/STL-10 training with 10% smudged, randomized-label images, reductions around epochs 60 and 120 coincide with falling abstention and worse validation performance.

ResNet-9/CIFAR-10 with 10% incorrect labels shows delayed mislabeled-example learning relative to a large fraction of examples under SGD, but joint learning and very low separation under Adam. ResNet18 without batch normalization on CIFAR10 with 15% wrong labels shows clean-first behavior in nonlinear and linearized regimes; noisy-label memorization begins at clean-example loss 1.25 for α=1 versus 1.5 for α=100. These loss coordinates do not themselves measure elapsed training time.

method_sensitivity.factor: Corruption level, available data and training budget
method_sensitivity.what: Early-stopped ResNet-20/CIFAR-10 loss distributions are approximately separable at 30% corruption; 50% increases clean-data loss and distributional overlap. Separately, arXiv:2101.06509 reports rowless MNIST mislabeled-data dominance especially above corruption fraction ρ=0.85. Pretrained wav2vec2.0 large at 5% training scale and 90% replacement reaches 29.8% peak test accuracy while exception memorization approaches 100%; direct corrupted-label fitting without a reliable preceding abstraction phase challenges V6. Cross-entropy ImageNet-PI high-noise training ignores wrong labels within 90 epochs, unlike later wrong-label fitting on CIFAR-10H/CIFAR-100N. The latter comparison changes dataset and noise source as well as the observation setting.

Excessive early strong augmentation in 18-layer PreAct ResNet training with 90% label noise impairs clean/noisy separation in normalized loss distributions at epoch 20, without establishing a full reversal; the Figure 2 dataset is unspecified. SimCLR pretraining delays noisy-example loss reduction for ResNet32/CIFAR-10 with 80% randomly flipped labels. The random-initialization control's noisy-loss curve alone does not establish relative clean/noisy learning order.

method_sensitivity.factor: Class balance, example complexity, annotation structure and image quality
method_sensitivity.what: With 10:1 ground-truth class imbalance and 30% flips, PreActResNet18 CE can favor an observed class rather than clean labels; evidence is an epoch-10 loss comparison. In a four-class MNIST/CIFAR-10 union with 10% noise, many complex clean CIFAR-10 examples learn as slowly as mislabeled examples. Without ADELE, segmentation categories are plotted separately: IoUel rises early then declines with category-dependent timing, with early learning reported for most PASCAL VOC foreground classes. Increasing IoUm alone establishes memorization without its order relative to early learning. The text tentatively links repeated bicycle/chair annotation errors to absent early recovery. In mixed retinal noise, mislabeled low-quality images have lower average loss than mislabeled high-quality images.

method_sensitivity.factor: Network depth, adapter rank and pretrained architecture
method_sensitivity.what: At approximately 30% CIFAR-10 corruption with Adam, the initial clean-first phase lasts about 100 epochs for MLP7/MLP5 versus 300 for MLP3. AG News rank-8 LoRA at 30% noise shows delayed noisy-loss reduction; Section 5.5 and Appendix B.2 additionally report that larger ranks shorten the delay, without an extracted rank-comparison row. In CoNLL03 fine-tuning, BERT, RoBERTa and DeBERTa exhibit fitting, settling and late noise-memorization phases, supporting V6. Noise level changes settling-phase duration, and RoBERTa is reported to resist late noise learning more than BERT and DeBERTa.

method_sensitivity.factor: Measurement definition, augmentation averaging and federated measurement location
method_sensitivity.what: Federated memorization outcomes differ between server/client measurements and heterogeneity settings; the supportive FedAvg trajectory specifically concerns the server. Checkpoint-based noise detection depends on detector and scheduler; prediction-recall decline is an indirect memorization measure. MNIST pristine/corrupt loss-reduction contributions cross at 25% and 50% randomization but not at 75%, despite directly reported faster pristine learning. The qualification of sampled mean cumulative contributions covers these noise conditions collectively. Fixed rather than averaged augmentations change SimCLR memorization profiles, but retained random-label rows do not isolate that intervention. Augmented random-label profiles occur at epochs 278, 373 and 421; epoch 12 belongs to the unaugmented condition.

method_sensitivity.factor: Synthetic problem structure and optimization regime
method_sensitivity.what: Under the noisy-XOR ReLU theorem, all clean and flipped training labels are correctly classified after the first step, before generalizable cluster features emerge; smaller step size delays both overfitting and generalization. In modular addition, GELU noisy loss decreases faster early, which cannot determine V6 learning order; a rowless ReLU result reports memorization before grokking. MNIST regression readily fits radial-wave noise at fixed k=0.1 but learns the true target before noise at fixed k=1; these panels vary amplitude β. Separate frequency sweeps fix β=0.5 or β=1. With noisy teacher outputs, MNIST inputs delay clean-MSE deterioration until thousands of epochs, whereas Gaussian inputs rapidly interpolate. These synthetic comparisons have different assumptions and are not matched replications.

status_amendment.public_note: This status now names the conditions where some studies find clean and noisy labels learned together or in reverse order: pair, asymmetric and feature-dependent label noise, adversarially chosen labels, very high rates of random noise, and two synthetic settings (XOR and modular addition). The level stays R2 (independently reproduced) for randomly corrupted labels below very high noise rates, because none of these results is a failed replication under matching conditions.
